examples.en: Sticky resin oozed out of the pine tree.

examples.ko: 손에 송진이 묻어서 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: I got pine resin on my hands and it won't come off easily.
People rub resin on a violin bow.
When we entered the forest, it was full of the smell of resin.
If you leave resin for a long time, it hardens.
Resin slowly flows from the wound in the tree.

explain: 소나무에서 나오는 끈적한 액이라서 옷이나 손에 묻으면 잘 안 지워져요. 바이올린 활에 바르는 것도 송진으로 만들어요. 소나무 숲의 냄새를 말할 때 '송진 냄새'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: When I entered the forest, I smelled pine resin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소나무 숲의 냄새를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the smell of a pine forest.

phrases.example: 옷에 송진이 묻어서 세탁해도 안 지워져요.
phrases.en: Pine resin got on my clothes and won't come out even after washing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈적해서 잘 안 지워진다는 말과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears with the idea that it is sticky and hard to remove.

phrases.en: I rub rosin on the violin bow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 활이나 운동 도구에 바를 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when applying it to an instrument bow or sports equipment.

explain_en: It is the sticky sap from pine trees, so it is hard to wash off clothes or hands. The rosin used on violin bows is made from it too. People talk about the smell of a pine forest as '송진 냄새'.

examples.en: The dung beetle rolls dung and carries it home.
I saw a picture of a dung beetle in an insect book.
The kids searched the meadow to find a dung beetle.
These days it's not easy to see a dung beetle.
I heard that dung beetles are very strong.
The dung beetle in the fairy tale is cute.

explain: 똥을 굴리는 모습이 먼저 떠오르는 곤충이라 동화나 곤충 책에서 만나요. 같은 곤충을 '소똥구리'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The book called it a 'sottongguri'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 곤충을 부르는 다른 표기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another spelling for the same insect.

phrases.en: I saw a dung beetle in the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충을 셀 때 '마리'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the counter 'mari' when counting insects.

phrases.en: The children are observing a dung beetle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업이나 체험 학습에서 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in science classes and field trips.

explain_en: This is an insect whose image of rolling dung comes to mind first, and you meet it in fairy tales and insect books. The same insect is also called '소똥구리'.

examples.ko: 피가 우리 몸 안을 계속 순환해요.
examples.en: Blood keeps circulating inside our body.
This bus loops around downtown.
Water circulated through the sea, sky, and land.
The air doesn't circulate, so the room feels stuffy.

examples.ko: 이 노선은 순환해서 같은 곳으로 돌아와요.
examples.en: This route is a loop, so you come back to the same place.
Seeing the seasons cycle around is amazing.

explain: '돌다'는 빙 도는 모든 움직임에 쓰는 일상 말이고, '순환하다'는 피, 물, 공기, 버스 노선처럼 돌아서 처음으로 되돌아오는 흐름에 써요. 과학이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I took a bus that circles around downtown.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순환하다'를 명사 앞에서 쓰면 한 바퀴 돌아 처음으로 오는 노선을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it describes a route that goes around and returns to the start.

phrases.example: 창문을 열면 방 안의 공기가 순환해요.
phrases.en: If you open the window, the air in the room circulates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공기나 물처럼 흐르며 계속 움직이는 것에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things like air or water that keep moving in a flow.

phrases.example: 피가 잘 순환하지 않으면 손발이 차가워요.
phrases.en: If blood doesn't circulate well, your hands and feet get cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘 ~지 않다'로 흐름이 좋지 않을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 'doesn't ... well' pattern describes a poor flow.

explain_en: To move around and return, like water, blood, or buses. 돌다 is the everyday word for any spinning motion; 순환하다 is for flows that go around and return to the start, such as blood, water, air, or a bus loop. You often see it in science and news.

en: to ripen; to become ripe; to mature

examples.en: In autumn, the grain ripens plump and full.
The chestnuts are fully ripe, so they taste good.
I picked a well-ripened pumpkin and made porridge.

examples.ko: 아이가 어른스럽게 여물어 가는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The child seems to be maturing and growing up.
The spring fruit hasn't fully ripened yet.
I wait until the seeds are fully formed.

explain: 열매나 곡식에는 '익다'보다 알맹이와 씨가 단단하게 꽉 찬 상태를 강조해요. 그래서 '여문 밤'처럼 속이 알찬 것에 잘 어울려요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '여문, 여무니, 여뭅니다'가 되고, 사람에게 쓰면 속이 단단하고 야무지게 자란 모습을 말해요.

phrases.example: 가을에는 여문 열매를 딸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: In autumn, you can pick ripe, full fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여물다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꿔 속이 단단히 찬 열매를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, describing fruit that is firm and full inside.

phrases.en: The corn kernels have filled out well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식이나 열매의 알이 단단하게 찼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the grains or kernels have filled out firmly.

phrases.en: That child is mature inside even though he is young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 생각이 깊고 야무지다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person, it means thoughtful and sensible.

explain_en: For crops and fruit, it stresses the kernel or seed filling out firm, whereas '익다' stresses becoming ready to eat. That is why it suits things that are solid inside, like '여문 밤'. The ㄹ drops, giving '여문, 여무니, 여뭅니다', and said of a person it describes someone who has grown up solid and capable.

t90.ax: I wait until the seeds are fully formed.

examples.en: Even a single cell is a living organism.

examples.ko: 숲은 여러 생물이 서로 영향을 주는 하나의 유기체 같아요.
examples.en: A forest is like one organism in which many living things affect each other.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 유기체와 무기물의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class, I learned the difference between organisms and inorganic matter.

examples.ko: 회사를 하나의 유기체로 보는 관점도 있어요.
examples.en: There is also a view that sees a company as one organism.

examples.ko: 이 박테리아는 아주 작은 유기체지만 영향이 커요.
examples.en: This bacterium is a tiny organism, but its influence is big.

examples.ko: 유기체는 환경이 바뀌면 거기에 적응하며 살아가요.
examples.en: Organisms adapt and live on when the environment changes.

explain: 생물학에서는 살아 있는 개체를 가리키고, 사회나 조직이 부분들이 서로 연결되어 움직인다는 비유로도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '생물'이라고 말해요. '무기물'과 짝으로 배우는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 흙 속에는 눈에 보이지 않는 살아 있는 유기체가 많아요.
phrases.en: There are many living organisms in the soil that you can't see.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생물학 설명에서 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing in biology explanations.

phrases.en: An amoeba is a single-celled organism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세포가 하나인 생물을 설명할 때 쓰는 학습용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A study term used to describe living things with one cell.

phrases.en: Many kinds of living things live in the ocean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유기체' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word used instead of 유기체 in daily conversation.

explain_en: Biology term, formal; a living thing seen as an organized system. In biology it refers to a living individual, and it is also used as a metaphor for a society or organization whose parts work together. In daily talk people simply say '생물'. It is often learned as a pair with '무기물' (inorganic matter).

t90.ax: Even a single cell is a living organism.

examples.en: Moonlight shone softly over the lake.

examples.ko: 잔잔히 흐르는 음악을 들으며 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book while listening to gently flowing music.
He nodded with a quiet smile.
The rain fell gently, and my mind felt at ease.
The teacher continued the story in a calm manner.
I like the sound of waves rolling in gently.

explain: 물결, 소리, 미소, 감정이 조용하고 고요할 때 쓰는 부사예요. 일상 대화에서는 '잔잔하게'도 많이 쓰고, 반대로 거칠고 세찬 모습은 '거세게'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The lake sparkles calmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잔잔히'와 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 잔잔히 and more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: I feel at ease when I listen to quiet music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '잔잔하다'의 꾸미는 말 모양이에요. 음악, 바다, 분위기 앞에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of the adjective 잔잔하다, often placed before music, sea or mood.

phrases.en: Grandmother smiled quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 웃지 않고 조용히 웃는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes smiling softly rather than laughing loudly.

explain_en: Gently quiet scenery, water or music (잔잔히 흔들리다) This adverb is for waves, sounds, smiles or feelings that are quiet and calm. In daily talk '잔잔하게' is also common, and the opposite, rough and strong, is '거세게'.

t90.ax: He nodded with a quiet smile.

examples.en: This plant purifies the air.

examples.ko: 정수기는 물을 정화해서 마시기 좋게 만들어요.
examples.en: A water purifier cleans the water so it is good to drink.

examples.ko: 강물을 정화하려면 시간과 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Purifying river water takes a lot of time and money.

examples.ko: 산책을 하면 마음을 정화하는 기분이 들어요.
examples.en: Taking a walk makes me feel like my mind is being cleansed.

examples.ko: 공장 폐수를 정화한 뒤에 강으로 내보내야 해요.
examples.en: Factory wastewater must be treated before it is released into the river.

examples.ko: 음악이 마음을 정화할 수 있다고 믿어요.
examples.en: I believe music can cleanse the mind.

explain: 공기, 물, 마음처럼 더러워진 것을 깨끗하게 만들 때 써요. 물건 표면을 닦는 일에는 '닦다', '청소하다'를 써요. '공기 정화', '정화 장치'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Walking in the forest purifies my mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정화하다'의 피동형으로, 저절로 깨끗해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form is used when something becomes clean by itself.

phrases.en: They installed a water purification device at the factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '정화'는 '장치' 같은 말과 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun is often paired with words like '장치'.

phrases.en: This machine makes water clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정화하다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way to say '정화하다'.

explain_en: To remove dirt from water, air or places, physical and neutral. Used for air, water, or the mind when something dirty is made clean. For wiping a surface, use 닦다 or 청소하다. The noun form appears often too, as in 공기 정화 and 정화 장치.

en: to penetrate; to go through; to transmit

examples.ko: 빛은 유리를 투과해서 방 안까지 들어와요.
examples.en: Light passes through the glass and comes into the room.
Ultraviolet rays can penetrate clouds.

examples.ko: 투과하는 빛의 양에 따라 렌즈 색이 달라져요.
examples.en: The lens color changes depending on the amount of light that passes through.

examples.ko: 엑스레이는 몸을 투과하기 때문에 안쪽을 찍을 수 있어요.
examples.en: X-rays pass through the body, so they can capture the inside.

examples.ko: 비닐은 물이 투과하지 못하게 막아 줘요.
examples.en: Plastic film keeps water from passing through.
It is hard for sound to pass through a thick wall.

explain: 빛, 소리, 전파, 방사선처럼 눈에 안 보이거나 흐르는 것이 물체를 뚫고 지나갈 때 쓰는 과학적인 말이에요. 사람이나 차가 지나갈 때는 보통 '통과하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '뚫고 지나가다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Ultraviolet rays cannot pass through a thick wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 어떤 물체가 빛이나 전파를 막는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form, used to say that an object blocks light or radio waves.

phrases.en: X-rays go through the body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '투과하다' 대신 쓸 수 있는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday substitute for 투과하다.

phrases.en: Light passes through the glass window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '투과하다'보다 쓰임이 넓어서 사람이나 차에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 투과하다; it also works for people and cars.

explain_en: Light, rays or liquid passing through a thin material. This is a scientific word for things like light, sound, radio waves and radiation passing through an object. For people or cars passing through, '통과하다' is the usual word. In daily talk people also say '뚫고 지나가다'.

examples.en: I lost my balance and almost fell.

examples.ko: 수영할 때는 물속에서 평형을 잡는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: When swimming, it is important to keep your balance in the water.

examples.ko: 저울의 양쪽이 평형을 이룰 때까지 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: Please wait until both sides of the scale are in balance.

examples.ko: 귀에 문제가 생기면 평형 감각이 떨어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If something is wrong with your ears, your sense of balance can get worse.

examples.ko: 그 위에 물건을 더 올리면 평형이 깨져요.
examples.en: If you put more things on top of it, the balance will break.

examples.ko: 생태계의 평형은 한번 깨지면 되돌리기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once the balance of an ecosystem is broken, it is hard to restore.

explain: '균형'과 뜻이 가깝지만 '평형 감각', '화학 평형'처럼 의학·과학 말투에서 많이 써요. 일상에서 몸이나 마음의 균형을 말할 때는 '균형을 잡다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 귀는 평형 감각에도 중요한 역할을 해요.
phrases.en: The ear also plays an important role in the sense of balance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 균형을 느끼는 능력을 말하는 의학·과학 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medical or scientific term for the ability to sense body balance.

phrases.en: I suddenly felt dizzy and lost my balance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 균형을 잃고 비틀거릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body loses balance and wobbles.

phrases.en: The scale is staying balanced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양쪽이 균형 잡힌 상태를 계속 지킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when both sides stay in a balanced state.

explain_en: Bodily or physical equilibrium (평형 감각) It is close to '균형' (balance), but '평형' is used mostly in medical and science contexts, such as '평형 감각' (sense of balance) and '화학 평형' (chemical equilibrium). In everyday talk about body or mind, '균형을 잡다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I lost my balance and almost fell.

examples.en: The government is trying to modernize the outdated facilities.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 짧은 기간에 산업을 근대화했어요.
examples.en: That country modernized its industry in a short time.
A project to modernize rural areas has begun.
Some people say the military needs to be modernized.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 설비를 근대화한 뒤 생산량이 늘었어요.
examples.en: After this factory modernized its equipment, output increased.

examples.ko: 학교 교육을 근대화하자고 주장한 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: There were people who argued for modernizing school education.

explain: '~을 근대화하다'처럼 대상이 필요한 말이에요. 사회, 산업, 제도, 시설을 옛날 방식에서 새 방식으로 바꿀 때 쓰고, 명사 '근대화'로도 많이 말해요. 공장이나 설비 이야기에서는 '현대화하다'도 같이 써요.

phrases.en: That city was modernized quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근대화하다'는 누가 바꾼다는 느낌이고, '근대화되다'는 바뀐 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 근대화하다 implies someone changes it; 근대화되다 states the result of the change.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 오랜 노력 끝에 근대화를 이뤘어요.
phrases.en: That country achieved modernization after long effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '근대화'와 '이루다'를 함께 써서 성공한 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 근대화 with 이루다 describes a successful result.

phrases.en: We modernized the hospital equipment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 쓰는 최신 방식으로 바꿀 때 써요. 시설이나 장비 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for changing to current, up-to-date ways. Fits talk about facilities and equipment.

explain_en: To bring society or things into the modern era; historical, formal. It takes an object, as in '~을 근대화하다'. It is used when changing a society, industry, system or facility from an old way to a new one, and the noun '근대화' is very common too. For factories and equipment, '현대화하다' is also used.

t90.ax: A project to modernize rural areas has begun.

en: to be stern; to be harsh

examples.ko: 이것은 어디까지나 현실이며 냉엄한 삶 그 자체예요.
examples.en: This is reality through and through, and life in all its harshness.
Reality is harsher than you think.
You have to survive in the harsh competition.
We have to accept the market's unforgiving judgment.

examples.ko: 냉엄한 현실을 알고 나서 더 열심히 준비했어요.
examples.en: After learning how harsh reality is, I prepared even harder.
The referee applied the rules strictly and without mercy.

explain: 현실, 경쟁, 평가처럼 사정을 봐주지 않는 상황에 어울려요. 사람의 차가운 태도에는 '냉정하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '냉엄하다'는 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 취업 시장의 냉엄한 현실을 알게 됐어요.
phrases.en: I came to know the harsh reality of the job market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사정을 봐주지 않는 현실을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for a reality that shows no mercy.

phrases.en: The world of competition is truly harsh.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 상황의 엄격함을 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for stating how strict a situation is.

phrases.en: The judges evaluated the works strictly and without mercy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봐주지 않고 엄격하게 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for evaluating strictly, without going easy.

explain_en: It suits situations that show no mercy, such as reality, competition or evaluation. For a person's cold attitude '냉정하다' is more common, and '냉엄하다' often appears in writing and news.

t90.ax: Reality is harsher than you think.

examples.en: The diversification of values is progressing quickly.
Opinions have become more varied because of the pluralization of society.
Thanks to the pluralization of media, there is more to watch.

examples.ko: 공급처 다원화를 위해 여러 나라와 협력하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to cooperate with several countries to diversify our sources.

examples.ko: 다원화는 좋지만 갈등도 늘어날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Pluralization is good, but conflicts may increase too.
We had a discussion about the pluralization of education.

explain: '다양화'와 비슷하지만 다원화는 중심이나 가치, 체계가 하나가 아니라 여러 개가 된다는 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '일원화'예요. 주로 사회, 문화, 미디어 이야기에서 써요.

phrases.en: Society is becoming more and more pluralistic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중심이 여러 개로 늘어나는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a change where there are more and more centers or values.

phrases.en: Opinions have become very different because values have become more varied.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in discussions about society.

phrases.en: We live in a pluralistic society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가치가 함께 있는 사회를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a society where many values exist together.

explain_en: Society, values or culture becoming plural, social or political. It is close to '다양화', but 다원화 suggests that centers, values or systems become multiple rather than one. The opposite is '일원화'. It is mainly used when talking about society, culture and media.

examples.en: Working in step with my colleagues makes it much easier.
They released a new menu to keep up with the trend.

examples.ko: 학교와 부모님이 발맞추면 아이가 잘 자라요.
examples.en: When school and parents work together, the child grows well.

examples.ko: 달리기 연습할 때 발맞추는 게 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to keep in step when practicing running.

examples.ko: 세계 흐름에 발맞추려면 영어 공부가 필요해요.
examples.en: To keep pace with the world, you need to study English.
The team members couldn't coordinate, so the work got delayed.

explain: 발걸음을 같게 한다는 데서 나와서, 지금은 속도나 방향을 맞춘다는 비유로 많이 써요. '~에 발맞춰'가 자주 나오는 모양이고, 비슷한 말로 '보조를 맞추다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I walked in step with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 걸음을 맞출 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used for actually matching steps.

phrases.en: We need to keep pace with our teammates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이고 조금 더 격식 있게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and sounds a bit more formal.

phrases.en: We move forward in step with the times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 같은 방향으로 가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes moving together in the same direction.

explain_en: It comes from walking in step, and today it is mostly used figuratively for matching speed or direction. '~에 발맞춰' is a very common form, and '보조를 맞추다' is a similar expression.

examples.en: The small fishing village was transformed into a tourist spot.

examples.ko: 그 도시는 해마다 아름답게 변모하고 있어요.
examples.en: That city is becoming more beautiful every year.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 만난 친구가 완전히 변모해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the friend I met after a long time had completely changed.
There are plans for the factory district to be turned into a park.
I captured the changing look of the city in photos.

examples.ko: 이 거리는 밤이 되면 전혀 다른 모습으로 변모해요.
examples.en: This street changes into a completely different look at night.

explain: '변하다'보다 겉모습이나 성격이 크게 달라질 때 써서 글과 뉴스에 많이 나와요. '관광지로 변모하다'처럼 '로'와 함께 바뀐 결과를 말해요. 작은 변화에는 '변하다'나 '바뀌다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I was surprised at my hometown's transformed look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 달라진 겉모습을 말할 때 쓰는 꾸밈말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier used for a look that has changed greatly.

phrases.en: The old factory was transformed into a cultural space.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변모하다와 뜻이 비슷하고, 완전히 새로운 모습이 될 때 쓰며 말할 때도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 변모하다, used when something becomes completely new, and it also sounds natural in speech.

phrases.en: Our neighborhood has changed a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 변화든 큰 변화든 두루 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, general word used for both small and big changes.

explain_en: Formal, gradual change in look or character of places or people. Compared with 변하다, it is used when appearance or character changes greatly, and it appears often in writing and news. It takes 로 for the result, as in 관광지로 변모하다. For small changes, people use 변하다 or 바뀌다.

t90.ax: That city is becoming more beautiful every year.

en: to co-exist; to stand side by side

examples.en: The two systems have existed side by side for a long time.

examples.ko: 전통 시장과 대형 마트가 병립하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy for traditional markets and big supermarkets to coexist.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 의견이 병립할 수 있는 사회가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like a society where differing opinions can coexist.

examples.ko: 옛 건물과 새 건물이 병립하고 있어서 독특해요.
examples.en: Old and new buildings stand side by side, which makes it unique.

examples.ko: 두 정당이 병립하는 구조라서 선거가 치열해요.
examples.en: Two parties stand side by side in this structure, so elections are fierce.

examples.ko: 두 가지 이론이 병립하면 학생들은 헷갈릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If two theories exist side by side, students may get confused.

explain: 'A와 B가 병립하다'처럼 '와/과'와 함께 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나오고, 말할 때는 '같이 있다', '나란히 있다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 동네에는 절과 성당이 병립하고 있어요.
phrases.en: In that neighborhood, a temple and a cathedral stand side by side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘 이상이 함께 자리 잡고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes two or more things standing together in the same place.

phrases.example: 두 가지 방식은 한 회사에서 병립할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: The two methods cannot coexist in one company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 있기 어렵다는 부정적인 뜻으로 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative use meaning they can't exist together, common in writing and news.

phrases.example: 한 골목에 옛집과 새 건물이 나란히 있어요.
phrases.en: An old house and a new building sit side by side on one street.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병립하다'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say what 병립하다 means.

explain_en: Formal — two systems or things standing side by side. It is used with '와/과', as in 'A와 B가 병립하다'. It shows up in news and writing; in speech people say '같이 있다' or '나란히 있다'.

t90.ax: I like a society where differing opinions can coexist.
